questions.question: To check the automatic transmission fluid level in some vehicles, the vehicle:

options.text: May need to be left running.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to be left running.
questions.explanation: In some vehicles, you need to leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: When using a turn signal, you should not:

options.text: Cancel the turn signal after completing the turn.
Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is complete.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the turn signal on long after the turn is complete.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep signaling until the turn or lane change is done. Then turn off the signal so other drivers are not confused.

questions.question: Hydroplaning usually occurs:

options.text: Where water collects on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where water collects on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens where water collects on the road. Low tire pressure or worn tires make it more likely. Hydroplaning can happen at speeds as low as 30 mph if there is enough water on the road.

questions.question: What is the only way to sober up after drinking?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers, coffee, and exercise cannot speed this up. The only way to sober up is to wait for the alcohol to leave your body.

questions.question: Check ____ to make sure air flows to all tires in your vehicle's air braking system.
questions.correctAnswerText: Before a trip
questions.explanation: Check the air brakes on double or triple combination vehicles during your pre-trip inspection. Wait for normal air pressure. Push in the red trailer air supply knob to send air to the emergency lines. Use the trailer hand brake to send air to the service line. Open the rear shut-off valve. If air escapes through the valve, the system is working.

questions.question: If a truck's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The truck will have no brakes.
The truck should only be driven slowly.
The truck will still have brakes.
The truck will lose brakes on its left side.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: If the ABS system fails, the truck will still have normal brakes. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, pressure of at least ____ should build up in both systems.
questions.correctAnswerText: 100 psi
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, allow the air compressor to build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: Air pressure in a dual air brake system should build from 85 to 100 psi within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 45 seconds.
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle moves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off right away.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, all warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately. This includes the charging circuit, oil, coolant, and Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) lights.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?

options.text: Between three-quarters of a second and one second

questions.correctAnswerText: Between three-quarters of a second and one second
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is between three-quarters of a second and one second.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Shoes with oil or grease on them
Pads with no oil or grease on them

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads with no oil or grease on them
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads with oil or grease on them, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn too thin. Pads that are clean and dry are in good condition.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection:

options.text: Helps catch small problems before they become big problems.
Should not be done by the driver.
Should be done once a month.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps catch small problems before they become big problems.
questions.explanation: Inspect your vehicle before every trip. Finding a small problem before you drive is better than discovering a big problem while you are on the road.

questions.question: A vehicle inspection:

options.text: Should only be done once a week.
Should only be done if the driver feels qualified.
Should be done by a friend.
Should be done before every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done before every trip.
questions.explanation: Every driver should inspect their vehicle before every trip to make sure it is safe to drive.

questions.question: With low beam headlights on, you can see about ____ ahead of your vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: 250 feet
questions.explanation: Low beam headlights let you see about 250 feet ahead. At night, drive slowly enough to stop within the distance your headlights show.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a possible cause of a vehicle fire?
questions.correctAnswerText: Rolling down the window
questions.explanation: Vehicle fires can be caused by spilled fuel, under-inflated tires, electrical problems, smoking near fuel, improper fueling, and flammable cargo that is not properly sealed or loaded. Rolling down a window cannot cause a fire.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Keep your eyes on the road ahead.
Look only to the front and right.
Look only to the front and sides.
Look to the front, sides, and rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the front, sides, and rear.
questions.explanation: Safe driving means being aware of everything around your vehicle. Watch the road ahead and check your mirrors often to see what is beside and behind you.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Assume the other driver doesn't see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver doesn't see you.
questions.explanation: When passing a pedestrian or another vehicle, assume they do not see you. This keeps you alert and safe.

questions.question: To release a dolly's air brakes before coupling it, you should:

options.text: Remove the dolly parking brake control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the air tank petcock.
questions.explanation: Open the dolly air tank petcock to release the air brakes. This is the first step when moving the dolly in front of the rear trailer.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue while driving, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool.
questions.explanation: A warm, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open the windows or vents, or use air conditioning to keep the cab cool and help you stay alert.

questions.question: If one air system in a dual air brake system loses pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
Lights on the outside of the tractor will flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, if one system loses pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. Stop safely and have the system repaired.
